newsitem.title: FRANCE: Corsican separatist chief urges talks with Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Corsican separatist chief urges talks with Chirac.

text.p: A Corsican separatist leader said on Friday he preferred President Jacques Chirac's style to that of Prime Minister Alain Juppe and was open to negotiations with the French head of state.

But in a sign the government might be more interested for now in cracking down on Corsican violence than in negotiations, a dozen people were taken into custody in Paris and Corsica in connection with the bombing of a golf course on the Mediterranean island on Thursday, justice sources said.
The sources said the 12 were being held on suspicion of attempted extortion and mounting an attack with an explosive material.

Francois Santoni, the leader of Cuncolta Naziunalista, the legal wing of the banned Corsican National Liberation Front (FLNC), said in a television interview aired on Friday, "As far as we are concerned, we are always open to a dialogue (with Chirac) because no one likes violence."
"At no time did he talk about 'terrorists'," Santoni said, praising Chirac's granting a marathon television interview on Thursday aimed at reassuring voters unhappy with his policies.
Santoni, who has gone into hiding to avoid answering to charges of arms violations, made the remarks in an interview with France 3 television videotaped in a secret location.

The FLNC said in a statement this week it planned "new forms" of attacks on the mainland in its campaign for increased autonomy from mainland France, in retaliation for Juppe's determination to crack down on the movement.
"Since Juppe has opted for a military solution...we have decided to adapt our struggle on the ground with increased resources," the FLNC's hardline "historic wing" said.
Juppe has pledged to crack down on the guerrillas and restore order, while proposing sweeping tax breaks for Corsica as part of a plan to revive the economy, create jobs and defuse violence.

The FLNC has said it was responsible for a spectacular blast that wrecked Juppe's mayoral office in Bordeaux on October 5 as well as bombs in other cities in an attempt to carry its struggle to the mainland.
The FLNC on Thursday claimed responsibility for the bomb attack at the golf course, which destroyed a house but injured no one.

Five armed and masked men burst into the house of the Sperone golf course's keeper and blew it up with dynamite after forcing the keeper and two unidentified people who were with him to leave, police said.
The seaside golf course of Sperone has been hit by several blasts in the past, for which the FLNC also claimed responsibility.
